item.title: EYES TO THE SKY: Celestial numbers in the spirit of Valentine’s Day
item.description: It’s 11 o’clock on a clear, moonless night when, although ready to call it a night, I pause at a glass door that looks out to the southwestern sky: I am moved by an urge for contact with the stars.

item.title: I WITNESS: Naming stuff after yourself is easier than you think!
item.description: Who could resist the opportunity to name a bunch of stuff after themselves?

item.title: THE OTHER SIDE: More quackery
item.description: For the life of me, I am unable to find a single justification for the Trump administration’s war on science, on rationality, and their refusal to accept the continuing need to expand opportunity to educate, train, and expand our pool of doctors and nurses and medical researchers.

item.title: ‘Joy and Play,’ a round-up of February school vacation week activities in the Berkshires
item.description: Whether your family is vacationing or “stay-cationing” in the Berkshires over the February school vacation, there are events to keep you entertained and inspired all week long!

item.title: CAPITAL IDEAS: The EU-India trade deal — Should you sell America and buy foreign stocks?
item.description: The EU–India trade agreement is a long-term re-routing of growth and capital, not a trading opportunity. The EU and India have effectively created a more predictable investment corridor by lowering trade frictions and modernizing rules around services, digital trade, and intellectual property.

item.title: TECH & INNOVATION: Why innovation needs continuity
item.description: People think innovation is about breaking things. It distinctly is not. Continuity is required to make anything stick long enough to be adopted.

item.title: BUSINESS MONDAY: Spotlight on Barrington Hall in Great Barrington
item.description: New owners, familiar address: The former Crissey Farm space is reborn as a flexible performance venue and community hub for private, corporate, and curated events.
